Motorcycle Glove Buying Guide

Choosing the right gloves depends on when and how you ride. Our flowchart guides you through season and style to the perfect pair.

Summer Gloves

Vented leather or mesh for airflow. Race gloves for track use with knuckle sliders.

Winter Gloves

Heated gloves for extreme cold or insulated touring gloves with Gore-Tex waterproofing.

All-Season

Waterproof touring gloves for year-round use or short-cuff sport gloves for versatility.

Key Features

  • CE certification for impact protection
  • Knuckle protector — hard or soft
  • Palm slider for abrasion resistance
  • Touchscreen-compatible fingertip
  • Visor wipe on left index finger
  • Secure wrist closure
keyTakeaways: Glove choice depends on when and how you ride, split into summer, winter and all-season types.
Summer gloves use vented leather or mesh for airflow; race gloves add knuckle sliders.
Winter gloves range from heated options for extreme cold to insulated Gore-Tex touring gloves.
Waterproof touring gloves are the most versatile all-season choice.
Look for CE certification, a knuckle protector, palm slider and touchscreen fingertips.

faq.q: What are the most important features in a motorcycle glove?
faq.a: Look for CE certification for impact and abrasion protection, a hard or soft knuckle protector, a palm slider to resist abrasion in a slide, and a secure wrist closure so the glove stays on in a crash. Touchscreen-compatible fingertips and a visor wipe on the left index finger are useful everyday extras.

faq.q: Do I need different gloves for summer and winter?
faq.a: Ideally yes. Summer gloves prioritise airflow with vented leather or mesh, while winter gloves need insulation and waterproofing to keep hands warm and functional. Cold, wet hands lose dexterity, which affects braking and clutch control. Many riders own a summer pair and a winter pair, or an all-season waterproof glove as a compromise.

For regular winter riding in temperatures near or below freezing, heated gloves are transformative. They keep fingers warm and responsive far longer than insulation alone, which matters for safe control. They cost more and need a power source, but if cold hands are cutting your rides short, they are a worthwhile upgrade.

faq.q: What are the best all-season motorcycle gloves?
faq.a: Waterproof touring gloves with a breathable membrane such as Gore-Tex handle the widest range of UK conditions, keeping hands dry in rain and reasonably warm in the cold while remaining wearable in milder weather. Short-cuff sport gloves offer a more versatile fit if you value feel over maximum weather protection.

Gloves should be snug with no loose material at the fingertips, yet still allow you to work the controls comfortably. Too loose and they bunch up and can come off in a slide; too tight and they restrict circulation and dexterity. Try them on and operate a lever or twist grip to check the fit before buying.
